A walk_away action on ANY thread ends the WHOLE case (see arena_kit/sim.py near line 363). The play loop (arena_kit/play.py, function `play`) answers all open threads concurrently and may call decide several times per round with a "view" where threads with our message in flight end with a buyer message; agents must be stateless or snapshot-safe (play's `_snapshot` only saves dict/list/set attributes). The parent class and helpers are in arena_kit/agents/reciprocal.py; the wrappers GuardedAgent (arena_kit/guard.py) and EvidenceAgent (arena_kit/agents/evidence.py) wrap FinalAgent in cli.agent_factory as EvidenceAgent(GuardedAgent(FinalAgent()), data, questions=False).

Intended behaviour of FinalAgent (check the code does exactly this, and find cases where it does not):
1. Never return a walk_away while any live thread still has a priced sheet or can still be asked for one. Silent suppliers (no priced sheet) are asked for a quote at most `max_asks` (2) times, then skipped. Only when no open thread is left does it call `closing_move` (accept the best acceptable sheet, else walk away).
2. Never counter a thread whose latest status is final_offer or agreed (closing_accept may accept it; otherwise work other threads or closing_move).
3. Anchor: when case["type"] == "price_increase" and buyer current_unit_price exists: max(0.75 p, min(p, cur)); otherwise max(0.75 p, min(0.80 p, cur or p)).
4. Steps: with match=None the step is the schedule step max(frac * (p - last), MIN_STEP * p, tick) without the MATCH throttle; with match=x it is throttled like the parent with x in place of MATCH. Price never above their price minus KEEP (5%) before the last two messages; never below our previous offer; never the same sheet twice.
5. Last message (moves_left == 1) must be an accept or closing_move, never a counter that could time out.
6. Everything else identical to ReciprocalAgent.

Review of FinalAgent. I ran pytest and ruff, and ran small snippets for the behaviours below. I read final.py, reciprocal.py, the relevant parts of play.py (`play`, `closing_move`, `latest`, `live_threads`, `moves_left`), guard.py (`_decide`, `_keep_going`, `_last_move`, `_counter`, `_eligible`, `_hopeless`) and evidence.py (`_rewrite`). I did not read sim.py, cost.py, docs.py or the rest of test_final.py (only its first ~80 lines).

Results
- `uv run pytest -q`: 249 passed, 53 skipped.
- `uv run ruff check arena_kit/agents/final.py`: 4 errors, all E501 (line > 120) at final.py:50, 64, 66 and 81.

Critical

1. final.py:54 (also :70) calls `closing_move`, which crashes when any thread has no supplier message (play.py:120 `live_threads` calls `latest`).
   - `_live` filters such threads out, so decide's early checks pass. But `closing_move` then runs `live_threads(threads)` over all threads, and `latest(ev)` raises StopIteration on the empty one.
   - Reproduced: `{"A": [reply(body="x"),ASK,reply(body="y"),ASK,reply(body="z")], "B": []}` raises StopIteration from `FinalAgent().decide`.
   - Under GuardedAgent the exception is caught. `_keep_going` then calls `closing_move` and crashes again, so the fallback ends in `_walk(...)`. That ends the whole case while thread B's opening may still arrive.
   - Fix: in `FinalAgent` (and ideally in `closing_move`/`live_threads`), pass `{s: ev for s, ev in threads.items() if _sup(ev)}` to `closing_move`. Make `live_threads` use `_sup(ev) and ...`. If a thread has no supplier message yet and our message is not in flight, do not close; ask for the quote or wait.
   - Related, same root cause: the empty-live path at final.py:40-41 returns walk_away when only empty threads exist. A walk_away ends the whole case. GuardedAgent does the same at guard.py:111. Reproduced with `{"B": []}`. This is unlikely in play because `_open` presumably excludes such threads (I did not read `_open`), but it breaks intent 1.

Major

2. GuardedAgent counters a final_offer thread when FinalAgent legitimately walks (intent 2 is broken in the wrapped agent that actually ships).
   - Scenario: A is final_offer at 60 with lead_time 52 (unacceptable), and B is silent and exhausted (skipped). FinalAgent returns `closing_move`'s walk_away. The guard sees "delegate wanted to walk" and calls `_hopeless` (guard.py:259). It returns False because B is not final and has moves left. The guard then picks the eligible thread via `_eligible`, which allows final_offer threads one counter (cap=1), and sends a counter to A at their price with must-haves fixed.
   - Reproduced with `GuardedAgent(FinalAgent())`: it returned a term sheet for `sup:A` at 60.0 / lead 42. That counter is not checked against the alternative's C.
   - So the only walk_away FinalAgent can produce is `closing_move`'s (no other path), but the guard can convert it into a counter to a dead final_offer thread. The guard also never asks silent B for a quote.
   - Fix: have `_hopeless` ignore threads FinalAgent has skipped. Alternatively, in `_keep_going` for "delegate wanted to walk", prefer asking an open non-final thread for a quote. Or make the guard check that the counter beats the alternative's C before sending.

3. final.py:42-70 does not guarantee intent 5 (the last message is an accept or closing_move) on its own.
   - `closing_accept` requires strict `c < c_open` (reciprocal.py:139), while `closing_move` accepts when `c <= c_open`. If the supplier holds its opening sheet to the end, so the standing sheet C equals the opening C, FinalAgent counters at moves_left==1 and the counter can time out.
   - Reproduced on P05 with the supplier holding 30.0 and moves_left=1: FinalAgent sent a counter at 29.0, not an accept of 30.
   - The GuardedAgent `_last_move` (guard.py:195-207) rescues this: a counter priced below theirs on the last move is replaced by `closing_move`'s accept. In the shipped wrappers the result is therefore OK.
   - FinalAgent alone is wrong. A counter priced at or above theirs would not be rescued, though the `_price` cap makes that rare.
   - Fix: in `decide`, `if any(moves_left(case, threads[s]) == 1 for s in open_)` (or for the chosen sid), return `closing_move(...)` before building sheets.

Minor

4. final.py:50, 64, 66, 81: E501 line length. Wrap them, or add `# noqa: E501` as the repo does elsewhere with `# fmt: skip`/noqa.
5. final.py:85: price_increase anchor `max(0.75p, min(p, cur))` ignores KEEP. If the supplier's price has already dropped to or below `cur` (for example in a view where `p <= cur`), the first counter equals their price, so we concede everything on message one. This is intended per the spec but worth a test.
6. final.py:35-37: `__init__` does not call `super().__init__`. This is harmless today because ReciprocalAgent has none, but it is fragile. The `_snapshot` helper only saves dict/list/set attributes. `match`, `anchor` and `max_asks` are immutable scalars set once, so snapshot-safety is fine.

Verified OK
- Thread with no supplier messages and another open thread: no crash (`empty+open` returned a counter on A).
- Multi-supplier case with one final_offer sheet (unacceptable) and one open thread: FinalAgent counters the open thread only, with no walk_away and no counter to the final thread (`final+open`).
- Single sheet with lead 52 on P05: the counter sheets have lead_time 42, and payment_days and lead_time_days are present with allowed values. Anchor is 0.80 x 30 = 24.0.
- Concurrent play loop: in the pending view, our in-flight message adds to `len(_mine)`, so fewest-messages-first avoids pending threads. If it still picks a pending thread, play.py:271-275 re-decides among free threads. If all threads are pending, play.py:260 breaks before calling decide. Any action decided while threads are pending is discarded (play.py:279-281). The re-decide call passes a subset view without the pending threads. In that view `closing_move` may produce a walk_away, but it is discarded under `pending`.
- `closing_move` `live_threads(threads)[0]` IndexError: not reachable from FinalAgent. `_live` being non-empty guarantees at least one live thread, and the only extra failure is the empty-thread case in item 1.
- Anchor and step formulas match the spec for intents 3 and 4. With `match=None` there is no throttle, and with `match=x` the throttle is `max(MOVING_MIN*p, tick, min(step, x*move))`. The cap uses KEEP while `moves_left > 2`, and `max(mine[-1], ...)` prevents going below our previous offer. Repeat-sheet avoidance is inherited from `_sheets`.
- evidence.py: with `questions=False` the must-have asks and the "send us your quote" ask are kept. The cost-breakdown and limit-reason questions are skipped. The default `questions=True` is unchanged. `__getattr__` guards the new `questions` attribute against recursion.
- cli.py and `__init__.py` registration is correct. The wrapper nesting matches `EvidenceAgent(GuardedAgent(FinalAgent()), data, questions=False)`.

   - Fix: in `FinalAgent` (and ideally in `closing_move`/`live_threads`), pass `{s: ev for s, ev in threads.items() if _sup(ev)}` to `closing_move`. Make `live_threads` use `_sup(ev) and ...`. If a thread has no supplier message yet and our message is not in flight, do not close; ask for the quote or wait.

   - Fix: in `decide`, `if any(moves_left(case, threads[s]) == 1 for s in open_)` (or for the chosen sid), return `closing_move(...)` before building sheets.
